Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (AE), Rohit Malhotra (SE), Maya Ortiz (PM), Elena Brooks (SRE), Liam Patel (Product), Sofia Gomez (Eng Mgr), Noah Kim (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Quick sync on roadmap launch readiness for v1.3. Main risk areas: performance on long-context, canary rollout config, monitoring & SLOs, rollback/runbook. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Perf validation on Dedicated and Hosted variants
- Canary rollout strategy and automatic fallback
- Alerting thresholds and SLO burn rate policies
- Documentation and customer communications
- Open risks (model regressions, infra quotas)

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: okay, uh thanks everyone for joining on time, we'll kick off, this is the roadmap launch readiness, uh product eng sync for v1.3, try to keep to the agenda, Maya do you want to kick off with the checklist?
[00:28] Maya: yeah sure, um quick recap — launch checklist is in the shared doc, I added owners for monitoring, canary, perf, and docs. main open items: perf numbers from staging, canary routing policy, SRE runbook final review.
[00:46] Rohit: I ran a quick smoke on the new kernel changes, saw about a 6 to 8% latency improvement at p95 on short forms but long-context heavy workloads still have variance, the KV cache warmup looks okay but there's some thrashing on the dedicated pool when we hit multiple concurrent long sessions.
[01:14] Elena: the thrashing, is that due to the cache TTL or connection churn?
[01:20] Rohit: looks like KV cache eviction is a bit aggressive, TTLs are 30s by default, with the new batching it exposes more cache churn. I can tune TTL and re-run. Also noticed GPU memory fragmentation causing small OOMs in the dedicated nodes under synthetic load.
[01:45] Sofia: are those OOMs reproducible? we need deterministic repro to file the bug with infra.
[01:52] Rohit: semi-repro; under 500 concurrent tokens generation with 8k context they pop, I'll produce a deterministic job by tomorrow.
[02:05] Liam: on the customer side, product asked if we can guarantee no regressions in quality when quantizing — legal ops also wants a clear rollback plan if we see quality drop.
[02:22] Maya: yes, rollback playbook is itemized but we need SRE signoff for the triggers. Elena can you confirm the SLO thresholds that should trigger an automated rollback?
[02:33] Elena: right now we have three buckets — latency, error rate, and quality (via eval hooks). For latency I'm proposing 3x p95 baseline or 200% increase in tail for 10 min window, error rate 1% absolute increase, for quality we need eval-set drift > 4% on key prompts. But the quality metric requires offline eval runs and it's slower to detect.
[03:03] Maya: okay that seems reasonable, but product needs a clear mapping of detection to action: who gets paged, who approves the rollback, and the auto-fallback targets (hosted -> dedicated or model variants).
[03:20] Avery: quick note, we should prefer automatic fallback to a smaller model variant before fully rolling back deploys — less churn. We discussed routing policy last week, can we confirm which variant is the primary fallback?
[03:33] Rohit: primary fallback is the same family quantized 8-bit variant; if that's not available, route to hosted smaller capacity model. There may be cost implications but it's safer.
[03:45] Noah: cost aside, product asked for a canary schedule that is conservative — 5% of traffic over 2 hours with progressive ramp. We need to ensure the canary's cache warm state and not underrepresent KV cache behavior.
[03:59] Rohit: yep that's the tricky bit, cold canaries hide cache behavior. We'll run a canary with synthetic warmup traffic and also a synthetic long-run to prime the KV cache.
[04:13] Maya: can you note that as an action? Rohit to run warmup canary and perf job.
[04:19] Avery: adding that.
[04:22] [05:00] Rohit: (background) also saw some metric name mismatch in the telemetry where kernel latency is labeled "krnlat" in one place and "kernel_latency_ms" elsewhere — it's making dashboards ugly. I'll align naming and push a small telemetry change.
[05:48] Elena: on alerting, we need to tune pager thresholds so on-call isn't paged for transient spikes. Propose a 10-minute window with three consecutive buckets before paging.
[06:06] Sofia: agree, and add a runbook step to mute noisy alerts for 30 minutes while we investigate to avoid pager storms.
[06:20] Maya: also, who will be primary for on-call during the launch week? we need a rotation.
[06:26] Elena: I'll coordinate with ops, Noah and I can cover the first two days, then hand over to the day shift team.
[06:34] Liam: marketing wants a short blurb for GA comms that highlights latency improvements and predictable throughput, but they can't promise numbers. Avery can you draft something with safe language?
[06:46] Avery: yeah I'll draft release notes, keep numbers high-level like "improved p95 latency for short requests" and call out dedicated clusters for enterprise. I'll share the draft by EOD tomorrow.
[06:56] [10:00] (discussion on rollout timeline)
[10:12] Maya: timeline still targeted for 2026-12-12 internal beta, GA 2026-12-20 pending signoffs. Any blockers to that?
[10:22] Rohit: the perf job and the dedicated pool OOMs are blockers; also we need validation for the kernel changes under mixed workloads.
[10:35] Elena: infra quotas for the dedicated cluster in eu-west-1 need increase requests — I've filed the cloud ticket but it may take 48 hours.
[10:46] Sofia: if quotas delay us, can we failover to another region for the canary?
[10:52] Rohit: yes but then we lose some latency baselines for EU customers; still doable as fallback.
[11:00] Maya: action: Elena will follow up on quota ticket and escalate if no response by EOD 12/06.
[11:05] Elena: noted.
[11:10] [20:00] (mid-call deep dive on perf numbers)
[20:22] Rohit: sharing numbers in chat — baseline p95 short is 120ms, new kernel shows 110ms, long context p95 is 680ms and after changes it's 640ms but variance is high. We should run a 24-hour soak to capture tail behavior.
[20:45] Liam: product wants to understand the customer impact — can we simulate a mixed workload that approximates our top 10 customers?
[20:54] Rohit: yes I'll create a workload mix from telemetry and run the soak in staging.
[21:01] Maya: put that in the checklist, owner Rohit, due 12/09.
[21:06] [30:00] (discussion about QA and eval hooks)
[30:12] Avery: on quality monitoring, the eval harness needs to run after each canary window, and we need a quick report that surfaces top regressions. Can we automate that?
[30:25] Rohit: yes, add an automated hook — the eval job is about 15 minutes, we can run it with synthetic prompts and key customer prompts. We should pin the model RNG seeds to reduce noise in quality checks.
[30:39] Maya: also include the human QA signoff step for any ambiguous regressions.
[30:45] Elena: ops note — make sure logs are retained for 30 days for initial beta for postmortem. Storage estimate is about 500GB for two weeks, we need approval for the cost.
[30:59] Sofia: finance has to sign off, Maya please add to the budget ask.
[31:05] Maya: will do.
[31:12] [40:00] (closing planning and runbook review)
[40:08] Avery: recap of owners: Rohit perf & canary runs, Maya final checklist & comms, Elena monitoring & rollback playbook, Avery draft release notes. Please confirm in chat.
[40:22] Rohit: confirmed.
[40:26] Maya: confirmed.
[40:30] Elena: confirmed.
[40:32] Liam: confirmed.
[40:35] [55:00] (some cross talk, minor interruptions)
[55:10] Maya: final question — do we want a customer-facing status page update during beta? it might prevent duplicate tickets.
[55:20] Avery: yes, put a short line on the status page about an upcoming beta and a link to the docs; ops to coordinate.
[55:30] Noah: I'll prepare the status page text and share it with Maya.
[55:34] Maya: thanks.
[55:40] [62:00] Avery: okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the checklist doc, I'll capture these notes and send out the meeting notes and next steps. If no other items, wrap up.
[62:12] (meeting ends)
